**Individuation** — what makes something one thing, and the same thing over time or across descriptions — individuation, numerical identity and diversity, individuality and persistence of things of any kind, biological individuality and organisational closure. Selves are self and persons are personhood (group: philosophy; ADR-015, ADR-024).

| [CLAIM-322](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-322.md) v2 | Agreement under a probe family is evidence that two objects share structure only to the degree that the family was chosen independently of the comparison and is evaluated on cases it was not chosen on, so a family selected to make two objects look alike shows only that it can be selected | Split from [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): its evidential half, stated on its own so that its warrant can be. | [CLAIM-360](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-360.md) v2 | The deep-versus-shallow learning results separate three effects that aggregate loss conflates: a larger realizable function class, a larger set reachable within a fixed data and compute budget, and a different internal organization with the same attainable outcomes; the deep linear results show the third, the random-hierarchy results the second, and the depth-separation result for products of inputs the first, at fixed size | The owner's, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's proposed experiment: "I think we may already have an empirical demonstration that would be useful here in the wide vs deep literature." | [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md) v4 | Whether a training-time regulatory condition belongs to a network depends on which unit is individuated for the training dynamics and whose jurisdiction governs the updates; in conventional training most of that governance falls to the optimizer–model–data system, so a condition of training is not thereby a condition of the network | The owner's correction, U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "it might help clarify things if we apply our individuation and volition frameworks to this system", the system being a deep network during training (U30). | [CLAIM-388](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md) v3 | Exact dynamical closure of a collective variable does not require a nearly decomposable block: in a linear Gaussian VAR(1) with uniform coupling among n units, the sum of all units is exactly dynamically independent at every stable coupling strength, while every partition of the units into two or more groups couples as strongly across its edges as within them | From A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, which gave the two-unit continuous-time case (ż = (b − a)z for z = x₁ + x₂) and the boxed slogan "Exact aggregation ⇏ near-decomposability". | [CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md) v2 | An individuation is well defined only once its criterion is fixed (the target it serves, the transformations its unity must survive, the scale), and that dependence does not make it arbitrary: once the criterion is fixed a verdict can be false, and differently fixed criteria can pick out units of one system whose boundaries cross rather than nest, none of them less real for it | The individuation counterpart of the owner's normative thesis [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) ("once they are fixed, the judgment can be false"), as A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 put it, on the owner's U8 question about "contextuality/relativity/subjectivity". | [CLAIM-417](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) v4 | What the record explained by "self" in its dispositional, persisting, self-governing and integrated senses is better explained by organizational perspectives, with a perspective, its carriers, its lineage and its representations kept apart; the subject sense stays a separate question, and narrative, presented and modeled selves involve representations that may describe a perspective, attribute it to a bearer or construct an owner, none of them the perspective itself | The owner's, at U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the record's earlier "selves" are "better described as 'organizational perspectives'". | [CLAIM-418](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md) v3 | Possessing, enacting or being shaped by an organizational perspective does not establish an independent agent, and perspectival, agential and institutional boundaries need not coincide: several agents can share a perspective, one agent can act through several, and a perspective can be reproduced with no agent governing it; where a perspective contributes to an agent's activity it can enable and constrain the exercise of agency, and that exercise can reproduce or transform it, while whether agency universally requires such a perspective stays open | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the owner's question at U38, "what's the relationship between perspective and agency?", A38's answer, and A39's request that it be recorded. | [CLAIM-420](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-420.md) v3 | A historical figure's influence can persist in three separable ways, as a story about them, as a perspective transmitted from them, and as later organizations that descend from their activity, and causal descent is not perspectival inheritance: a movement founded to oppose someone can descend from them without continuing their perspective | From the owner's U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, corrected. | [CLAIM-421](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md) v4 | The cessation of an organizational perspective's enactment need not imply the loss of the dispositions, capacities or reproductive relationships from which it can be reinstated: an interruption can be of activation (the disposition is held but not engaged or retrievable), of enactment (held, but the material, institutional or social conditions for exercising it are gone) or of reproduction (held by some bearers, but the processes that pass it on are damaged), and temporary unavailability is not extinction, though prolonged interruption of reproduction can end a tradition | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22, at the owner's U37: the doorway effect as perspective meeting grounded experience, and the perspectival interruptions of the Chinese Cultural Revolution. | [CLAIM-424](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-424.md) v3 | Reflexive governance of an organization's perspectival arrangements, making the conditions that govern its own interpretation, evaluation and action available for effective examination and revision, is a capacity some organizations of perspective have and others lack, not what makes something a perspective; and the capacity to revise those standards is not the capacity to revise them well | A37's definition, from the exchange of 2026-10-22, re-scoping [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md). | [CLAIM-454](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-454.md) v2 | A latent feature or mode recovered from an organization's members' activity is at most a constituent of an organizational perspective, not the perspective: a feature allocation says which members take part in which modes, and whether those modes are organized into one perspective depends on the relations of access, uptake and authority among their carriers, which the same allocation leaves open | From the Northstar turns of the exchange "Experimental Infrastructure Review", where the owner proposed inferring an organization's perspectives with hLDA (T21) and the Indian buffet process (T22). | [CLAIM-463](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-463.md) | Restoring the conditions under which a capacity was lost need not restore the capacity: where the activity that maintains it reinforces itself, the same conditions can sustain both the capacity and its absence, so a capacity lost past a threshold returns only under conditions better than those it was lost under, or by rebuilding the activity directly, and restoring it can cost more than preserving it would have | A4's claim candidate from the exchange "About the Chagossians" of 2026-10-26, "Resource restoration does not imply organizational restoration", which the first filing declined because [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md) already derives it; the owner asked for it to be filed as a claim with its connection to the case. The research program is to find the conditions for each, and their dependencies, apart from the order in which an inquiry meets them | Filed at the owner's review of the pull request, which asked for a synthesis "From Interconnection to Individuation: A Relational Constraint Research Program" that would make the theory "legible as a research program with distinct testable transitions, rather than a cluster of philosophically suggestive analogies". | [CLAIM-518](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md) v3 | Normative judgments about an organization's continuity, reform or obligations can depend on diachronic relations that descriptions of present states or terminal outcomes do not show, so specifying the relevant relations and histories can be necessary to apply them adequately; which continuations ought to follow is a further normative question, not a prerequisite of every normative judgment | From the owner's observation at U26 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), "normative judgements are only cognizable when they are relative to a judgement of whether some organization should persist or change", as narrowed at the owner's review the same day. | [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) v2 | Recovery under interventions on state cannot show where maintenance is realized: an outside controller that measures the constraint capacities and supplies the internal production law as state feedback yields the same trajectory under every perturbation of state, damage and recovery included, even with every capacity observed exactly; only interventions on the production mechanisms, relative to a declared boundary, separate the two | From A10 §4 (its Proposition 5) of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). | [CLAIM-525](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-525.md) v2 | Information in the sense the Simondonian readings give it, a disparity whose resolution reorders the system that takes it up, is in the line's terms a change in the interpreter or in the questions receivers can decide, not evidence about a fixed situation, so Blackwell's order leaves it out by construction and the two accounts are not rivals | The record's placing, on 2026-10-31, of the information concept in the Simondon readings (Iliadis 2013; Bencherki and Iliadis 2021; Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy 2024) against the line's Blackwell treatment. | [CLAIM-526](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md) v2 | Describing persons and organizations as coexisting levels of one process removes the question of how already-constituted agents add up to a collective, but not the question of levels: whether a collective variable has dynamics of its own, closed against the activity that realizes it, can be decided on a process description that presupposes no agents, is sometimes decided no, and a closed collective variable can be an aggregate that coexists with its realization while keeping none of its members' distinctions | Filed on reading Bencherki & Iliadis 2021 and Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy 2024, who hold that the "scaling up" problem "vanishes the moment communication is viewed eventfully" ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1364) because persons and organizations are "different informational levels that preserve all the characteristics of their organized components" ([LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), ms. p. 21, proposition 2). The record's closure results show what survives. What vanishes is the picture of agents adding up. What remains is whether a higher variable runs on its own, which is a question about variables and is decidable. The record's own case of a closed collective variable is a sum, an aggregate, that coexists with its units, so "stages or coexisting levels" is not a dichotomy. It does not say that the agent picture is right, or that organizations are aggregates of members. | Active |
| [CLAIM-529](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-529.md) v3 | An organization can be individuated without presupposing it as a declared candidate whose verdict can come out false: criteria stated on the candidate's interactions (whether benefit can be booked per member, which interactions the others depend on, what removing an interaction type does, whether its order survives release from an outside scaffold) apply to a grouping not yet assumed to be a unit, while criteria stated as members' attitudes toward the group (a goal about it, belonging, identity) make it partly constituted by being taken as one, individuating it by a different relation, unavailable where members have no such attitudes | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)). Their abstract says transitions in individuality are hard to describe without circularity, since the features used are products of the transition, and claims a non-circular description that the body never argues. The body holds the parts of an answer, and they are of two kinds. Criteria on interactions (per-member accounting of benefit, entrenchment order, knockout of interaction types, release from a scaffold) can test a declared candidate without assuming it is a unit ([CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md)), and the scaffold test needs the declared boundary ([CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)). Criteria on members' attitudes toward the group (shared goal, belonging, focal goal of sustaining it) individuate constitutively, which is not the non-circular route and is unavailable for organisms without such attitudes. It does not say the paper argues this, and it leaves the presupposed lower-level units where the paper leaves them. | Active |
| [CLAIM-530](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-530.md) v2 | Where maintenance is realized is a question of constitutive relevance only through its parthood condition: an internal producer and an outside controller supplying the same production law as state feedback meet mutual manipulability's two manipulability conditions identically, since disabling or stimulating either changes the maintained capacities and intervening on the capacities changes the activity of either, so what puts one inside and the other outside is parthood, a boundary the experiments presuppose and do not find | The record's join of [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) with the mechanist account of constitution, from Craver and Bechtel's admission that interlevel experiments are symmetrical and show componency only prima facie ([THEORY-1287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1287.md)). In [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s pair the bottom-up and top-down interventions come out alike for producer and controller. So the criterion separates them only by its parthood clause, which is [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s declared boundary. The criterion is cited as Baumgartner and Gebharter state it (LIT-1934, p. 8, read in full in NOTE-1493); Craver's own texts stay unread. It does not say no criterion can draw the boundary. | [CLAIM-531](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-531.md) v2 | Generative entrenchment does not by itself give organizational closure: an entrenched core, which later interactions depend on so that perturbing it is catastrophic and perturbing them tolerable, can sit at the root of an acyclic dependency order, and where interactions turn over such an order persists only while something outside supplies its core; an organization that is both entrenched and closed has a core containing a cycle of mutual maintenance, each interaction on which is itself core unless its share of the maintenance is redundant | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)), who mark the step from conexus to community by generative entrenchment of core interactions and then, with "Hence", by organizational closure.
